questions.q: Which of these facts about a function can its TypeScript signature actually express?
questions.explain: A readonly T[] parameter removes every mutating method from the array's type, so the compiler checks that promise. TypeScript has no effect system: reading the clock, logging and determinism are invisible to the types and stay a matter of convention.
options: It does not read Date.now()
It does not write to the log
It does not change the array it receives
It returns the same result every time for the same arguments

questions.q: Which call is referentially transparent, meaning you could replace it with its result everywhere without changing what the program does?
questions.explain: vatKobo(1000000) is always 75000 and does nothing else, so 75000 can replace it. The counter changes state, the charge has an effect in the world, and the delivery fee depends on a hidden input (the clock).
options: nextOrderNumber(), which increments a counter and returns it
vatKobo(1000000), which returns Math.round(1000000 * 0.075)
chargeCard(card, 5000), which calls a payment provider and returns a receipt id
deliveryFeeNow(), which reads the current hour

questions.q: A teammate wants to cache (memoise) a function's results. What must be true of the function for the cache to be safe?
questions.explain: A cache replaces later calls with an earlier result. That only preserves behaviour when the call could have been replaced by its result in the first place. A function that logs, or reads a price table that changes, gives wrong or missing behaviour when cached.
options: It must return a number or a string
It must be referentially transparent: same arguments, same result, and no effects that the cached calls would skip
Its parameters must be readonly
It must be declared with function, not as an arrow

questions.q: Given function addGift(lines: string[]): void and function count(lines: readonly string[]): number, which call does tsc reject?
questions.explain: Mutable fits readonly: count only promises not to change the array. Readonly does not fit mutable: addGift could push into an array its owner was promised would stay unchanged, so TS4104 refuses it.
questions.code:
const draft: string[] = ["RICE-5"];
const confirmed: readonly string[] = ["OIL-1"];
options: count(draft)
count(confirmed)
addGift(draft)
addGift(confirmed)

questions.q: Why is it a good default to type array parameters as readonly T[] when a function does not change them?
questions.explain: A readonly parameter accepts the widest range of callers and states a promise the compiler enforces inside the function. It changes nothing at runtime: the array is not frozen and runs at the same speed.
options: Readonly arrays are faster at runtime
It freezes the caller's array so nobody else can change it
Callers with mutable and readonly arrays can both call it, and the signature documents that their data is safe
It makes map and filter return readonly arrays

questions.q: With interface Line { sku: string; qty: number }, which line inside function f(lines: readonly Line[]) compiles?
questions.explain: readonly Line[] protects the array, not the objects inside it. qty is not readonly on Line, so changing it compiles. Mark the properties readonly too, or use a deep readonly type.
options: lines.push({ sku: "SALT", qty: 1 })
lines[0] = { sku: "SALT", qty: 1 }
lines[0].qty = 5
lines.sort()

questions.q: A plain JavaScript file imports your TypeScript function that returns a readonly string[]. What stops the JavaScript code from pushing into it?
questions.explain: Types are erased when TypeScript becomes JavaScript. readonly stops TypeScript code that sees the type. To make the runtime refuse, freeze the array, which throws a TypeError on push in strict mode code.
options: The readonly type: it is compiled into a runtime check
Nothing can; arrays are always mutable in JavaScript
Only a runtime mechanism such as Object.freeze; the readonly type is erased
Node.js type stripping, which keeps readonly at runtime

questions.q: Why is function pipe(...fns: Array<(x: any) => any>) a poor type for a pipe helper?
questions.explain: any switches checking off at every join and leaks into whatever uses the result. Overloads link each step's output type to the next step's input type, which is what makes swapped steps a compile error.
options: Rest parameters cannot hold functions
It compiles for any list of functions, so a step that does not fit the next one is never reported, and the result is any
It only allows up to four steps
It makes every step run twice

questions.q: The lesson's pipe has overloads for one to four steps. You need six steps. What keeps full type checking?
questions.explain: A nested pipe is itself a function from the first input to the third output, so it is a valid single step of the outer one. The implementation signature is not callable from outside; only the overloads are.
options: Cast the sixth step with as any
Nest pipes, for example pipe(pipe(a, b, c), d, e, f)
Call pipe with an array of the six functions
Use the implementation signature directly

questions.q: In which situation does an Option type fix something that T | undefined cannot?
questions.explain: (T | undefined) | undefined is just T | undefined, so two levels of absence collapse into one. Option<T> | undefined keeps them apart. For the other cases, T | undefined is simpler and fully checked.
options: Returning the result of array.find
An optional phone field on a customer
A cache of lookups whose result may itself be "no value", so "not cached" and "cached as nothing" must be told apart
A function parameter with a default value

questions.q: With type Maybe<T> = T | undefined, what is Maybe<Maybe<string>>?
questions.explain: Unions are sets, and a set containing undefined twice contains it once. The nesting vanishes, which is exactly why a two-level "maybe" needs a type with its own discriminant.
options: Maybe<string> | undefined, a nested type that remembers both levels
string | undefined
string | undefined | undefined, which TypeScript reports as an error
never

questions.q: Why does the lesson's mapResult take the function first and the result later, as mapResult(fn)(result)?
questions.explain: mapResult(priceLines) is a ready-made step that pipe can call with each result. "Configuration first, data last" is the same rule that made curried functions composable in Functional JavaScript.
options: TypeScript cannot infer generics when the result comes first
A pipeline step must be a one-argument function of the data flowing through, so the data has to be the last argument
It makes the function run faster
Results must always be the second argument of any function

questions.q: A cart has five lines, and each line is checked independently (known product, whole quantity above zero). Which error strategy suits the customer best?
questions.explain: When checks do not depend on each other, collecting all problems lets the customer fix everything in one round trip. Fail-fast suits dependent steps, such as reading a rate that can only exist after the JSON parsed. Dropping lines charges for a cart the customer did not see.
options: Fail fast with andThen, reporting the first bad line
Check every line and return all the problems at once, as a list in the error
Throw on the first bad line
Drop the bad lines and charge for the rest

questions.q: Where does a tryCatch(run, onError) helper belong?
questions.explain: It converts foreign exceptions into values where they enter your code. Pure core functions return Results directly. Programming errors (broken invariants) should still throw loudly rather than become ordinary values.
options: Around every function in the functional core
At the boundary with code that throws (JSON.parse, drivers, libraries), turning the throw into a typed Result
Only inside tests
Around programming errors, so the app never crashes

questions.q: How many different values does { paid: boolean; channel: "web" | "app" | "pos" } have?
questions.explain: An object type is a product: 2 values of paid times 3 values of channel is 6.

questions.q: How many different values does { kind: "none" } | { kind: "some"; value: boolean } have?
questions.explain: A union is a sum: the none member has 1 value and the some member has 2 (one per boolean), so 1 + 2 = 3. That is Option<boolean>: "the values of boolean, plus one".

questions.q: Promotions are an ADT (a discriminated union with one interpreter). Which change is easy in this design?
questions.explain: With an ADT, a new operation is one more function with a switch over the kinds. A new kind requires every interpreter to handle it (the compiler lists them). Functions have the opposite trade-off: this tension is the expression problem.
options: Letting another team plug in a new kind of promotion without touching your code
Adding a new operation over all promotions, such as describe or validate
Storing a promotion that contains a JavaScript function
Adding a new kind without updating any switch

questions.q: What can a promotion represented as an ADT do that a promotion represented as a function cannot?
questions.explain: An ADT value is plain data, so it survives JSON.stringify, can be listed and described, and validated. A function can only be called; its logic is opaque.
options: Run faster
Be generic
Be stored as JSON, shown to customers and checked by an admin screen
Be called inside a pipeline

questions.q: What does "parse, don't validate" change about the first step of the checkout?
questions.explain: A boolean check leaves later steps with a plain SKU and a lookup typed Product | undefined. Returning a richer type carries the proof in the data, and every later step can rely on it.
options: It throws instead of returning a Result
It returns true or false for the whole cart
It returns a new type (ValidCart) whose lines already hold the looked-up Product, so later steps never handle "not found"
It parses the cart from a JSON string

questions.q: Why does the build give each pipeline stage its own type (PricedQuote, DiscountedQuote, TaxedQuote…) instead of one Quote with optional fields?
questions.explain: With one wide type, addVat would accept a quote with no discount yet and would have to check discountKobo for undefined. Stage types turn the business order into a type error.
options: Optional fields are not allowed on readonly types
Each step can require exactly the fields earlier steps set, so a step in the wrong order does not compile, and no step checks for undefined
It makes the objects smaller at runtime
TypeScript cannot spread objects with optional fields

questions.q: The lesson says the stage types are only "partly" safe. Why?
questions.explain: Structural typing checks what a value looks like, not where it came from. Someone can write { ...quote, discountKobo: 0 } and skip the promotion step. The next lessons show how brands make a type that only one function can produce.
options: Because interfaces can be merged
TypeScript compares shapes, so any object with the right fields fits a stage type, even one not produced by the previous step
Because readonly is erased at runtime
Because overloads stop after four steps

questions.q: A test file contains // @ts-expect-error above quote.subtotalKobo = 0;. Someone removes readonly from subtotalKobo. What happens?
questions.explain: @ts-expect-error requires the next line to have an error. When the line starts compiling, the directive itself becomes the error. That is what makes it a test of what must not compile.
options: Nothing; the directive only silences errors
tsc fails with "Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive", so the test catches the lost guarantee
The assignment now throws at runtime
The test prints FAIL

questions.q: A function creates an empty array, pushes into it in a loop, and returns it as readonly T[]. Is it pure?
questions.explain: Purity is about what callers can observe. Mutating a local value that has not escaped is invisible from outside, and is often the fastest way to build a result.
options: No, because push is a mutation
Yes, if it has no other effects: it only changes data it created, which nobody can see before it returns
Only if the array is frozen before returning
Only if the loop is replaced by reduce

questions.q: The generic match(value, handlers) needs a cast inside. What is the honest way to live with it?
questions.explain: The compiler cannot link "the handler for this value's kind" with "this value". One contained cast behind a well-typed signature, pinned by tests, is a reasonable price; the same cast spread through application code is not.
options: Avoid generics and write any for the handlers
Remove the cast and add // @ts-ignore
Keep the cast inside one small, tested helper, so application code stays fully checked
Copy the cast into every place that calls match

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: toSorted returns a new sorted array and leaves the original alone, which is why it exists on readonly string[] while sort does not.
options: BEANS OIL-1 false
BEANS BEANS false
BEANS BEANS true
OIL-1 OIL-1 false

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A readonly type is a view through one reference. basket and view are the same array, and the mutable reference can still change it.
options: TypeError: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible

questions.q: This compiles. What does it print?
questions.explain: Object.freeze is shallow at runtime and its type, Readonly<…>, is shallow too: zones cannot be replaced, but the array inside is an ordinary mutable array.
options: TypeError: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible
undefined

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The cast removes the compile-time protection, but the runtime freeze still refuses: push throws a TypeError in a module (strict mode), and the array keeps its two zones.
options: true 2
added
false 3
true 3

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: get returns undefined both for a stored undefined and for a missing key; only has can tell them apart. That collapse is the bug an Option type prevents.
questions.code:
const cache = new Map<string, number | undefined>([["OIL-1", undefined]]);
console.log(cache.get("OIL-1"), cache.get("SALT"), cache.has("OIL-1"), cache.has("SALT"));
options: undefined undefined true false
undefined undefined false false
null undefined true false
undefined undefined true true

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: JSON has no undefined, so JSON.stringify drops the property. An Option value is an ordinary object and survives the trip, which matters when absence must be stored or sent.
options:
{"sku":"OIL-1"}
{"sku":"OIL-1","discount":{"kind":"none"}}

{"sku":"OIL-1","discount":undefined}
{"sku":"OIL-1","discount":{"kind":"none"}}

{"sku":"OIL-1","discount":null}
{"sku":"OIL-1","discount":{"kind":"none"}}

{"sku":"OIL-1"}
{"sku":"OIL-1"}

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Voucher first: (1,000,000 − 200,000) × 1.075 = 860,000. VAT first: 1,075,000 − 200,000 = 875,000. pipe runs left to right, and the order of steps is a business decision the types alone cannot make for you.

questions.q: How many times does readRate run, and what is printed?
questions.explain: andThen skips the next step when the previous one failed, so readRate never sees the text that did not parse. '"high"' parses to a string, so readRate runs and rejects it.
options: 2 0.075 bad-json bad-rate
3 0.075 bad-json bad-rate
2 0.075 bad-rate bad-rate
3 0.075 bad-rate bad-json

questions.q: The build computes the best discount with Math.max(0, ...discounts). What does this print?
questions.explain: Math.max() with no arguments is -Infinity, which would poison every later sum. The leading 0 makes "no promotions" mean "no discount", and also ignores a negative discount from a buggy rule.
questions.code:
const none: number[] = [];
console.log(Math.max(...none), Math.max(0, ...none), Math.max(0, ...[-5, 170000]));
options: -Infinity 0 170000
undefined 0 170000

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Spread builds a new outer object but copies references: the lines array is shared, not copied. That structural sharing is why each pipeline stage is cheap, and why the shared parts must never be mutated.
options: false true 3
false false 3
true true 3
false true 2

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Every line is checked, and each returns zero or one problem, so all three bad lines are reported. A Set has no inherited keys, so "toString" is correctly unknown.
options: 3 toString: unknown
2 OIL-1: bad qty
1 TV-99: unknown
3 OIL-1: bad qty

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Two calls give 1 + 2 = 3; reusing one result (the third number) gives 3 + 3 = 6. Replacing a call by its earlier result changed the answer, so the function is not referentially transparent: it has a hidden input and a hidden output, the counter.

questions.q: Finish cheapest(lines, n): return the SKUs of the n cheapest lines by unit price, without changing lines (it is readonly, so sort is not available). The program should print SALT,OIL-1 RICE-5.
questions.explain: toSorted returns a sorted copy, so the caller's order survives (lines[0] is still rice). [...lines].sort(…) works too; both copy first.

questions.q: Finish mapOption and getOrElse for the Option type. The program looks up a product's discount and prints the discounted price, or the full price when there is no discount. It should print 765000 320000.
questions.explain: Checking kind narrows the option, so option.value is only reachable in the some branch. none has type Option<never>, which fits any Option<U> because it carries no value.

questions.q: Finish partition(results): split a list of results into the values and the errors, keeping their order. The program should print 2,5 | not a quantity: two; not a quantity: -1.
questions.explain: The function mutates two local arrays it created and returns them as readonly: still pure. Narrowing on result.ok gives value in one branch and error in the other.
questions.expected: 2,5 | not a quantity: two; not a quantity: -1

questions.q: Finish tryCatch(run, onError): it runs run() and returns an ok result, or, if it throws, an error result built by onError. The program should print ok 0.075 | error SyntaxError.
questions.explain: The catch variable is unknown, so onError receives unknown and must narrow it. The helper turns a throwing API into a value with a typed error, right at the boundary.

questions.q:
Finish describe for this payment ADT with an exhaustive switch (no default). The program should print:

card ending 4242
transfer from GTBank
cash on delivery, change for ₦5000
questions.explain: Each case narrows method to one member, so only its fields are available. With a string return type and no default, adding a fourth payment kind makes the function fail to compile until it is handled.
questions.expected:
card ending 4242
transfer from GTBank
cash on delivery, change for ₦5000

questions.q: A price is either a single item or a bundle of prices with a percentage off. Finish the recursive interpreter priceKobo. The program should print 1053000: a 10% off bundle of rice (₦8,500) and an inner 20% off bundle of two ₦2,000 salts.
questions.explain: The inner bundle is 400,000 × 0.8 = 320,000; the outer is (850,000 + 320,000) × 0.9 = 1,053,000. A recursive ADT has a recursive interpreter with the same shape: one case per member, recursion where the type refers to itself.

questions.q: Finish setQty(cart, sku, qty): return a new cart where that line has the new quantity. Everything is readonly, so build new objects. Lines you did not change must be the same objects as before. The program should print 1 3 true.
questions.explain: Only the objects on the path to the change are copied: the cart, its lines array and the oil line. The rice line is shared (structural sharing). Writing line.qty = qty would not compile, because the property is readonly.

questions.q: Finish the three-step pipe3 so that each step's output feeds the next. The types are already written; only the body is missing. The program should print ₦8600.00.
questions.explain: The body is one line, and no casts are needed: the type parameters already say that ab produces what bc consumes, so cd(bc(ab(a))) type-checks as a D. The parameter a gets its type A from the declared return type, by contextual typing.
